newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, spreads dominate trade.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, spreads dominate trade.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mixed on Monday as the July/November spread tacked on 13-3/4 cents per bushel amid ideas weather patterns were conducive to new crop development, traders said.

Old crop months drew strength from strong cash basis levels and speculation last week's declines would attract renewed buying interest. Traders said the market shrugged off bearish input from USDA's export inspections data.
USDA on Monday put weekly soybean export inspections at 5.5 million bushels. That figure was below trade estimates for eight million to 12 million bushels.
"I think the trade is starting to be concerned that these lower prices are going to start to build some demand," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities in Iowa.
Roose and others noted U.S. old crop supplies remained tight and the market needed to continue to ration demand.

"That number is history," a floor source said, referring to the export inspections. "This is a futures market. The bottom line is, we're going to start pricing ourselves back into competitive levels and we don't have the beans for that."
Soybeans ended 4-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 14 cents lower with July up 1-1/2 at $8.66 a bushel.
Soybeans had struggled most of the session with a bearish technical outlook and forecasts for good crop growing weather.

Technical traders said soybean charts had been giving off bearish signals since last Monday's sharp break, triggered by news USDA left unchanged at 125 million bushels its forecast for soybean ending stocks. Many analysts had expected a cut.
But support held in the July contract above $8.50 a bushel which triggered short covering and new buying interest.
"We held at $8.52 in the July, above last week's low of $8.51-1/2," a pit source said. "When the bears were unable to take out that low, that gave us our first bounce."
The July closed above the 4- and 20-day moving averages.

Forecasts for warmer temperatures this week and weekend rains were considered bearish for new crop and contributed to the declines. Traders said that outlook would be beneficial for germination and early crop development.

New crop was further weakened by ideas Monday's USDA weekly crop progress report would show the crop was roughly half planted as of Sunday. After the close of trading, USDA said 46 percent of U.S. soybeans were planted.
On the day, Rosenthal Collins was said to be the key player.

Rosenthal sold four million bushels July early but bought seven million July and sold seven million November, traders said. Rosenthal also spread 2.5 million bushels July/November at $1.56-1/2, premium July.
The spread closed at $1.68-3/4, premium July.
In options trade, Rosenthal bought 100 July $8.50 puts at 21-1/4 cents and CIS sold 300 July $8.50 calls at 26 to 28 cents, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 63,000 contracts, just under Friday's actual volume of 63,760 contracts.
